full_judgment: 4. It may be mentioned that the loanee asked for adjournment on different occasions on the round that he filed a criminal case against the personnel of the Bank and that the same having been dismissed he filed revision before the High Court Division and the same is pending. The Artha Rin Adalat rejected those petitions for adjournment and finally decreed the suit ex-parte on May 20, 2001. 5.It has been contended by the writ-petitioner that after the decree he obtained the certified copy and deposited half of the decretal amount and also purchased court fees but having had fallen ill could not file appeal within the prescribed period of limitation. 6. The High Court Division discharged the Rule on the finding that under Article 102(2) of the constitution the High Court Division is to consider whether the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat "suffers from coram non judice or there is allegation of malafide or fraud" and on consideration of the materials on record observed that any of the aforesaid conditions are absent as regard the proceeding of Money Suit No. 1 of 1996 of the Artha Rin Adalat, Tangail and as such calls for no interference. The High Court Division further observed that writ petitioner as per law was required to file appeal but did not do so alleging that he had fallen ill but no evidence was brought on record in support of the said alleged illness.
